briefing.headline: US-China AI chip export tensions escalate as OpenAI and xAI race toward 10^27 FLOP models

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs continue rapid scaling with OpenAI and Google DeepMind releasing major updates this week. US export controls on advanced chips are tightening while China accelerates domestic alternatives. Funding remains robust with multiple $1B+ rounds closed.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4-preview with enhanced multi-agent capabilities. Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus while Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B. xAI's Grok-3 reached internal benchmarks surpassing prior leaders on agentic tasks.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize red-teaming for autonomous agents amid rising jailbreak incidents.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced three new 100k H100 clusters in Texas and Arizona. TSMC reported 3nm yields improving for next-gen AI accelerators. Google's TPU v6 pods now online with 40% efficiency gains.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls successfully slow China's frontier model progress by more than 12 months by 2028?
